english.title: Drive conveyance ( not motor vehicle ) taken without consent
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a conveyance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CONVEYANCE..) had been taken without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, drove the said conveyance
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1) of the Theft Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing / believing that a conveyance had been taken
without the consent of the owner / other lawful authority
drove it

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This is a summary offence but sections 40 and 41 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 provide that this offence may be joined in an indictment and dealt with at Crown Court in certain circumstances.
(ii) See also offence wordings H430, H434, H435, H439 and H2108.
(iii) See also aggravated TWLA

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a level five fine on the standard scale on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
